scope.summary: Define the canonical BodyKit skeleton per Section 13.18 (BK-18.1, TAI-BK-057/058), closing the Part-3 skeleton contract and AREQ-014 stability: a custom skeleton UE5-compatible by construction (pelvis, spine_01..spine_05, neck_01, head, clavicle_l/r, upperarm_l/r, lowerarm_l/r, hand_l/r, thigh_l/r, calf_l/r, foot_l/r, ball_l/r, upperarm_twist_01_l-style twist bones) EXTENDED with first-class breast_l/r, glute_l/r, belly chains and full genital chains (penis_01..penis_05, scrotum_l/r, labia bone set, anus) as plain exportable bones — stored as a versioned bodykit_skeleton_defs (BSK-) row; ik_* bones are NOT in the authority skeleton (UE export profile only).
acceptance_criteria: SkeletonDef type holds the bone tree (name, parent, rest transform mm, orientation convention) and serializes to the bodykit_skeleton_defs skeleton_json layout; the canonical v1 skeleton is seeded with the exact UE5-overlap names and the extension chains listed in TAI-BK-057.

A conformance test asserts the seeded skeleton contains: all UE5-overlap names, twist bones for upperarm/lowerarm/thigh/calf, breast_l/r chains, glute_l/r, belly chain, penis_01..penis_05, scrotum_l/r, the labia bone set, and anus — and contains zero bones matching ik_*.

Versioning law (TAI-BK-058): rename/restructure attempts against an existing version are rejected without a major version bump; additive chain extension requires a minor bump; every dependent artifact type carries a skeleton_version field.
Bone naming validation: snake_case with _l/_r side suffix convention enforced on insert.
Skeleton loads into the solver as a typed pose-ready hierarchy (parent indices resolved, no cycles).
scope.risk_if_missed: The skeleton is the content-compatibility contract for every pose asset, corrective, weight map, and export profile; an unstable or SMPL/Genesis-shaped skeleton would either legally poison the product or force UE-side rig surgery on every export — the Daz-bridge pain list BodyKit exists to delete.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Emits/extends the TAILOR_BODY_* KernelEventType family on the EventLedger per Section 13.16 (extends the 13.14 canonical list).
internal_diagnostics ships with WP-KERNEL-012; wire the open diagnostic-event API for this behavior in the WP-KERNEL-016 retrofit.
Palmistry external watcher ships with WP-KERNEL-012/016; long generation/bake/export runs get child-stall watch coverage in the retrofit.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.
